hints: Start by writing out what actually forms when ammonium meets hydroxide, focus on proton transfer rather than redox.
You should get $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NaCl}$, now think about which of these are simple covalent molecules with polar bonds.
Compare the shapes of $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{NH}_3$ and track the oxidation number of N to eliminate the other statements.
walkthrough:
**Write the reaction equation**

Think of this as an acid-base reaction. $\text{NH}_4^+$ donates a proton to $\text{OH}^-$.

$$\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{NaCl}$$

**Identify the polar molecular products**

Both $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ are small covalent molecules with very electronegative N and O atoms. Both have a net dipole, so both are polar.

$\text{NaCl}$ is ionic, not a polar molecule, so we have exactly two different polar product molecules.

**Check the nitrogen species**

In $\text{NH}_4^+$, N is tetrahedral with bond angle $109.5^\circ$. In $\text{NH}_3$, N is trigonal pyramidal with bond angle about $107^\circ$ due to the lone pair. The angle decreases.

Oxidation state of N stays at $-3$ in both $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{NH}_3$, and $\text{NH}_4^+$ acted as an acid by donating $\text{H}^+$, not a base.

options.A: Correct. The molecular products are $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Both are polar due to N-H and O-H bond dipoles and their asymmetric shapes. $\text{NaCl}$ is ionic, so there are two different polar product molecules.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4^+$ is tetrahedral ($109.5^\circ$) with no lone pair on N, while $\text{NH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal (about $107^\circ$) with one lone pair that compresses the angle. Students who forget lone pair repulsion may think the angle is unchanged.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4^+$ donates a proton to $\text{OH}^-$ to form $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so it acts as a Bronsted-Lowry acid, not a base. The base here is $\text{OH}^-$.
options.D: Incorrect. Oxidation state of N in $\text{NH}_4^+$ is $-3$ ($x + 4(+1) = +1$) and in $\text{NH}_3$ is also $-3$ ($x + 3(+1) = 0$). This is acid-base, not redox, so no change occurs.
